claims.text: As-cast eutectic high-entropy alloys have a relatively coarse lamellar microstructure.
The as-cast alloy contains residual stresses.
Intermediate-temperature annealing can induce partial recrystallization in as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Intermediate-temperature annealing can produce a more uniform precipitate distribution.
Appropriately selected annealing temperature and time can reduce residual stress without causing complete recrystallization.
The annealing treatment will reduce lamellar spacing.
The annealing treatment will create a fine, uniformly dispersed population of secondary precipitates.
The annealed microstructure will enhance dislocation storage.
The annealed microstructure will produce more balanced plastic deformation and improve strain distribution.
Fine precipitates and refined microstructural boundaries will increase strength through precipitation and grain-boundary strengthening.
Improved strain distribution will increase ductility.
Intermediate-temperature annealing will simultaneously increase yield strength and ductility relative to the untreated as-cast alloy.
Yield strength and ductility may each improve by approximately 10–20%.
Excessively high annealing temperatures or long annealing times can cause over-coarsening or loss of dual-phase benefits.
Annealing at too low a temperature or for too short a time may be insufficient to refine the microstructure.
The magnitude of the annealing response depends on the specific alloy composition.
